items.title: 10.2.2 Finding the oxidation number of an element in a compound or a radical

source_refs.note: Topic 10.2.2 with Sample Problems 10.1 to 10.3 and Quick Check 10.1, printed pages 215-216.

blocks.text: The oxidation number or state of any atom of an element present in a compound or a radical can be determined by making use of the above-mentioned rules.
Compounds of a metal with a non-metal
A metal always has the positive Ox. No. and nonmetals have the negative Ox. state For example, in sodium sulfide, Na₂S:
Compounds of a non-metal with a non-metal
In compounds containing two different non-metals, the sign of the Ox. No. depends on the electronegativity of each atom. The most electronegative element is given the negative sign.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 10.1
blocks.problem: Find the oxidation No. of S in Sulfur dioxide, SO₂.
steps: Ox. No. of each O atom = –2

blocks.text: Compound ions are ions with two or more different atoms. Examples are the sulfate ion, SO₄²⁻, and the nitrate ion, NO₃⁻.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 10.2
blocks.problem: Calculate the oxidation number (Ox. No.) of sulphur in SO₄²⁻.
steps: [Ox. No. of S] + 4 [Ox. No. of O] = -2
blocks.answer: Thus, the oxidation number of sulphur in SO₄²⁻ is +6.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 10.3
blocks.problem: Calculate the oxidation number (Ox. No.) of manganese in KMnO₄.
steps: (Ox. No. of K) + (Ox. No. of Mn) + 4 (Ox. No. of O) = 0
blocks.answer: Thus, the oxidation number (Ox. No.) of Mn in KMnO₄ is + 7.
